findings.title: Named balance assertion (opening + Sigma mvts = expected) is under-proven — J-3 asserts only finiteness + a tautology
findings.evidence: Wave J KEY ASSERTION = 'balance = opening + cash-in − cash-out ± collects (no skew)'. The test that claims to prove it (J-3 'balance math on reconciled session') computes expectedDerived = opening + signedSum (L306) but then NEVER compares it against the rendered 'Montant attendu' (65,50 €) cell. Lines 313-314 assert only Number.isFinite(expectedDerived) and Number.isFinite(variance). Line 320-322 builds closingReconstructed = expectedDerived + variance and asserts closingReconstructed >= 0 — a tautology: closing is DEFINED from opening+signedSum+variance, so the check passes for ANY numbers regardless of DOM consistency. The author explicitly abandoned the real cross-check, commenting 'Locate the expected cell by its sibling <dt> label text is brittle across locales' (L309-312). So the spec's headline numeric guarantee is not actually enforced.
findings.product_impact: NONE this run — I verified the DOM math by hand and it closes exactly (50.00 + 15.50 = 65.50 = Montant attendu; variance 0.00 = 65.50 − 65.50). This is purely a TEST coverage gap: a future regression that skews expected vs opening+Σmvts would slip past J-3 silently.
findings.fix_hint: In J-3, read the 'Montant attendu' <dd> (it has a stable adjacent <dt> 'Montant attendu' — the label is i18n-stable in this FR-only V1, and the cell is the <dd> immediately after that <dt>). Assert parseFrMoney(expectedCell) toBeCloseTo(opening + signedSum, 2), and assert variance toBeCloseTo(closingCell − expectedCell, 2). That turns the headline assertion from finiteness into the actual identity.

findings.title: 'Clôturer la caisse' button: white text on pale bg-warning — label invisible in render (cash action)
findings.evidence: On the OPEN session detail (Caisse Livreur #2... actually #1c shows an Ouverte session), the screenshot shows an empty white rounded rectangle where the close button sits. DOM confirms it is NOT empty: <button type="button" class="db-btn bg-warning text-white" data-testid="delivery-cash-action-close">Clôturer la caisse</button>. The label exists but renders white-on-pale-warning, so it is visually unreadable in the capture (contrast well under WCAG AA 4.5:1). Contrast vs the clearly-legible orange 'Ouvrir La Caisse' (white on #F4501E) and 'Annuler' buttons in J-2.
findings.product_impact: Sighted operator sees a blank button for the primary mutation on a CASH surface (closing a delivery-boy float). Functional (label is in DOM, reachable by keyboard/SR), but an embarrassing/confusing visual defect on a money screen. measured-P1 candidate downgraded to P2 because the text is present and the action path is not blocked.
findings.fix_hint: DeliveryBoyCashSessionShowComponent.vue ~L77 — the close action uses 'db-btn bg-warning text-white'; bg-warning is too pale for white text. Use a darker warning token or dark text (e.g. text-dark / amber-600 bg) to reach >=4.5:1.

findings.title: 'Close locks further entries' proven only on RECONCILED, never on CLOSED-not-reconciled
findings.evidence: Wave J KEY ASSERTION includes 'close locks further entries'. The read-only run proves the RECONCILED (terminal) state is locked (action-close=0, action-reconcile=0 on J-3). But RECONCILED != CLOSED. The CLOSED-not-reconciled state — where the brief expects the close button gone but reconcile present — is only exercised in J-4 (skipped, J_RUN_DESTRUCTIVE unset). So 'close locks' (the transition close->no-more-close) is NOT demonstrated by any captured artifact this run.
findings.product_impact: NONE observed (no closed-not-reconciled session exists in the dirty dev DB to inspect). Coverage gap only.
findings.fix_hint: On a throwaway DB run with J_RUN_DESTRUCTIVE=1 J_LIVREUR_ID=<id> to capture J-4c-detail-closed and assert action-close hasCount(0) while action-reconcile is visible. Or seed a CLOSED (not reconciled) row for a read-only snapshot.

findings.title: Brief enumerates states with no implementation route — scope discrepancy (manual cash-in / cash-out / error close-with-unsettled)
findings.evidence: AUDIT_PLAN Wave J states list includes 'manual cash-in · cash-out · ... · error close-with-unsettled'. The spec header (L26-28) documents, from routes/api.php L674-690, that there is NO cash-in/cash-out/movement-mutation route — movements are auto-appended server-side by DeliveryBoyCashSessionService::recordMovement and never exposed in this UI. So those brief states are unrealizable against the actual implementation. 'error close-with-unsettled' likewise has no captured artifact.
findings.product_impact: NONE — it is a brief-vs-implementation scope mismatch, not a product defect. Documenting so the next reviewer does not flag the missing manual cash-in/out UI as a P0 gap.
findings.fix_hint: Reconcile AUDIT_PLAN Wave J state list with the read-only movement reality, or add a note that manual movements are out of scope for V1 (auto-entry only).

verdict_rationale: Zero product P0/P1. The CASH balance identity (opening + Σsigned mvts = expected; variance = closing − expected) holds exactly in the DOM and is consistent across list and detail — no numeric skew. No console errors, no unexpected 4xx/5xx, no i18n leaks, terminal (reconciled) session is fully locked with no leaked edit controls, status filters genuinely filter. The named balance assertion in the spec is under-proven (J-001, P2 audit_integrity) but the underlying DOM numbers actually agree, so per the reviewer protocol this is NOT a product P0. One visual contrast defect on the close button (J-002, P2) and two coverage gaps (J-003 P2, J-004 P3) round out the non-blocking list.
